scenes.title: Bluma Zeigarnik interrupting absorbed 1927 Berlin participants mid-puzzle while sweeping unfinished clay & bead tasks into a drawer

layout.description: Sunlit 1927 Berlin wood-paneled laboratory table arranged with tactile Weimar-era craft puzzles — a half-sculpted matte-white porcelain dog figurine, a half-strung wooden bead cord, a completed folded-paper star, and a wooden jigsaw frame — beside a deep oak desk drawer where interrupted tasks are swept out of sight.

positions.who: Bluma Zeigarnik (mannequin in 1927 tailored blouse, cardigan, and midi skirt)
positions.where: gently placing a palm between the volunteer and a 75%-finished wooden puzzle to interrupt right at peak absorption while sliding it into the oak drawer

positions.who: Participant mannequin (in 1920s knit vest and rolled sleeves)
positions.where: hands still hovering forward in mid-air longing to snap the final two puzzle pieces in, eyes tracking the drawer rather than the finished paper star on the table

props.name: half-finished jigsaw & clay sculpture vs completed folded paper star
props.period_detail: tactile hands-on tasks clearly contrasting 75%-done interrupted work with 100%-done completed work

props.name: deep oak 'Out-of-Sight' sweep drawer & 'Unfinished 1.9x Recall' ledger
props.period_detail: wooden table drawer hiding all materials before the surprise free-recall question
props.physical_behavior: proves mental tension — not visual cues — drives the ~90% recall jump

actions.verb_sequence: finishes folding the paper star and sets it aside calmly -> leans in deeply absorbed on the last pieces of the wooden jigsaw
steps in right before completion, sweeps the unfinished jigsaw into the closed drawer, and asks what tasks they remember -> Participant immediately names every unfinished task first

reactions.reaction: leans toward the closed drawer still mentally finishing the interrupted puzzle while barely recalling the completed star
records the 1.9-to-1 Unfinished/Completed recall ratio in her 1927 ledger

scenes.wardrobe: 1927 Berlin university attire: pleated midi skirt, collared blouse and cardigan; wool knit vest over crisp cotton shirt.
scenes.lighting: Warm, bright tall-window European laboratory daylight.
scenes.recognition_hook: Finish a puzzle and your mind drops it in seconds — snatch it away two pieces before the end and it dominates your memory nearly two to one.

key_visual.description: a 1927 researcher at a wooden workbench sweeping a nearly finished jigsaw puzzle and matte-white porcelain figurine into a drawer while a seated participant's hands still reach to finish it

scenes.title: Kurt Lewin's Berlin Cafe Waiter: Razor-Sharp Until Paid, Blank 30 Seconds Later

layout.description: Sunlit 1920s cafe terrace with marble-topped bistro tables, porcelain coffee cups, and pastry plates.

positions.who: Waiter mannequin in crisp white apron and bow tie
positions.where: reciting a table's six-person order effortlessly from memory, then shrugging blankly moments after closing the leather bill folder
leaning forward fascinated by the instant memory wipe upon payment

props.name: porcelain coffee service & closed leather billfold ('PAID')
props.period_detail: marks the exact psychological boundary between open tension and closed tab
props.physical_behavior: the real-world spark of the Zeigarnik Effect

actions.verb_sequence: recites complex order perfectly -> closes PAID billfold -> looks genuinely blank when Lewin asks to repeat it 30 seconds later

reactions.reaction: exchange an 'aha!' glance and open a research notebook

scenes.wardrobe: 1920s café waiter waistcoat and apron; academic tweed jackets.
scenes.recognition_hook: No notepad for two hours, 100% accuracy — until the bill is paid and the waiter's mental blackboard wipes itself clean.

scenes.title: TV Cliffhangers vs 25 Unplanned Open Browser Tabs

layout.description: Bright study desk contrasting twenty cluttered half-started sticky notes against a streaming screen freezing on 'TO BE CONTINUED...'

positions.where: feeling hooked by a single cliffhanger vs scattered by twenty half-finished tasks

props.name: 20 half-written sticky notes
props.period_detail: trigger intrusive attention pings during focus tasks
props.physical_behavior: shows the dark side of unmanaged open loops

actions.verb_sequence: tries to read one page while eyes keep darting back to unfinished task notes

scenes.recognition_hook: Storytellers weaponize one open loop to hook you — twenty accidental open loops at work hijack your evening peace.

scenes.title: The 60-Second Shutdown Plan ('Consider It Done', 2011)

layout.description: Sunlit tidy oak desk where a planner notebook sits beside a closed laptop.

positions.where: writing 'Tomorrow 9:00 AM — Draft Slide 4 at desk', closing the planner cleanly, and walking out relaxed

props.name: When-and-Where Shutdown Card
props.period_detail: satisfies the goal-tracking alarm without working until midnight

actions.verb_sequence: writes concrete time + place for remaining task -> closes laptop and smiles calmly

reactions.reaction: shoulders drop into genuine off-duty rest

scenes.recognition_hook: You don't have to finish a 10-hour project tonight — hand your brain a written 9:00 a.m. appointment and it closes the tab.
